plan.notes: Source: official NIU 'Computer Science - Software Development' Degree Path - Catalog 2024-25 (PDF), published by NIU's advising office, https://aac.niu.edu/advising/degree-paths/2024-2025/liberal-arts-sciences/computer-science-software-development.pdf. Transcribed manually from the official term-by-term sequence on 2026-09-30; course codes, titles, and credit values are exactly as published in the degree path. EMPHASIS: NIU's B.S. in Computer Science requires one of three emphases; this plan follows Emphasis 1, Software Development (the most general/standard emphasis), as published in the degree path. The other emphases are Enterprise Software and Computational Software. EDITION: catalog_year is 2024-2025, an archived edition (the current catalog at catalog.niu.edu is the 2025-2026 edition, effective Fall 2025). The 2024-2025 degree path is the newest term-by-term sequence obtainable from NIU; the 2025-2026 catalog's Emphasis 1 requirements list (CSCI 240, 241, 330, 340, 360, 463, 466, 467, 480 plus CS electives; MATH 206, MATH 211/229, STAT 200/300) agrees with the sequence used here. CREDIT ANOMALIES (documented, not invented around): (1) the degree path models CSCI 480 (Principles of Operating Systems) at 3 credits (its Semester 7 total is 15-16 on that basis), while the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 catalog requirement lists credit CSCI 480 at 4; modeled at the degree path's own value. (2) The degree path prints MATH 206 as 3-4 credits; the catalog lists it as 3; modeled at 3. (3) The degree path prints 'MATH 211 or 155' in Semester 3, but the catalog's actual requirement is MATH 211 OR MATH 229; modeled as the catalog's MATH 211/MATH 229 choice, at the degree path's printed 3 credits (catalog credits MATH 211 and MATH 229 at 4 each). (4) 'MATH 229 or Elective' (Semester 4) is printed as 3-4 credits and 'MATH 230 or Elective' (Semester 5) as 3; both modeled at 3 credits with the catalog's 4-credit course values documented in choice_note. UNIV 101 is printed as optional in the degree path ('UNIV 101 (optional)'); included at 1 credit with the optionality noted. STAT 300 instead of STAT 200 in Semester 6 requires MATH 229 and MATH 230 due to prerequisites, per the catalog. Choice slots (Knowledge Domain courses, electives, CS electives, calculus/statistics options) use distinct placeholder codes and count toward the 120-credit total; ranges are modeled at the degree path's printed values with catalog values documented in choice_note. Prerequisite chains were NOT transcribed from the course-description pages, so every prereq array is empty and external_prereqs is empty; nothing was invented.
